RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46). CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates. METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding. RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059). CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

title: Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering. RESULTS: Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14-0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16-0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23-0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

title: Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined. METHODS: We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models. RESULTS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets. CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

title: Association of Clonal Hematopoiesis Mutations With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has been linked to cardiovascular disease through inflammation-related pathways, but its association with atrial fibrillation (AF) remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to systematically review and meta-analyze evidence on the association between CH mutations and AF, with planned analyses by hematologic cancer status, variant allele frequency (VAF), mutations, and sex. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 6, 2026, for studies reporting adjusted quantitative associations between CH and incident AF. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Study quality was assessed using the Risk Of Bias In Non-randomized Studies-of Exposures tool. RESULTS: Five studies comprising 7 cohorts and 299,215 participants were included. In populations without cancer, CH defined by VAF ≥2% was not significantly associated with AF (HR: 1.02; 95% CI: 0.97-1.07; I2 = 0%). Large CH clones (VAF ≥10%) were associated with a modestly higher AF risk (HR: 1.11; 95% CI: 1.01-1.22; I2 = 0%). Mutation-specific analyses did not show statistically significant associations for DNMT3A, TET2, or ASXL1 individually, and no sex-based effect modification was observed. In hematologic cancer populations, CH mutations were significantly associated with higher AF risk (HR: 3.22; 95% CI: 1.02-10.13; I2 = 0%). Sensitivity analyses and wide prediction intervals warrant cautious interpretation, particularly for the VAF ≥10% and hematologic cancer analyses. CONCLUSIONS: The association between CH and AF may vary by clonal burden and hematologic cancer status. However, evidence remains limited and observational. Larger studies with standardized CH and AF definitions are needed to clarify clinical relevance.

title: Climate change: the patient perspective.
abstract: This article for the CardioPulse section dedicated to the Environment was written after an online interview with a selection of members of the ESC Patient Forum. It relates the impact of climate change and especially heat waves on their treatment and how the cardiology community could do better in instructing them.

title: Universal ECG Screening for School-Age Children: A Pediatric Cardiology and Public Health Perspective.
abstract: Sudden cardiac death in the young remains an important public health concern extending beyond competitive athletes. Recent advances, including the 2025 AHA/ACC (American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology) Scientific Statement, the 2024 CSRC (Cardiac Safety Research Consortium) Think Tank Report, pediatric electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation, disease-specific risk stratification and treatment, shared decision-making, and implementation strategies, provide a timely opportunity to reconsider the potential role of universal ECG screening in school-age children. This state-of-the-art review synthesizes contemporary evidence on the epidemiology, diagnostic value, ethics, implementation, and international experience of ECG-inclusive screening. The available evidence supports a contemporary framework for evaluating its value not only in preventing sudden cardiac death but also in facilitating earlier detection and management of childhood-onset cardiovascular diseases, with possible downstream benefits in mortality, morbidity, and health care burden. Future research should determine how universal ECG screening can be effectively implemented and evaluated across diverse health care systems.

title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined. AIMS: We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact. METHODS: This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood. RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

title: Preferential Conduction Along the Epicardial Ventricular Septum During Idiopathic Ventricular Arrhythmias Originating From the Basal LV Summit: A Pitfall for Anatomical Ablation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: An anatomical ablation of idiopathic ventricular arrhythmias (VAs) originating from the left ventricular summit (LVS) is delivered from endocardial sites across the myocardium adjacent to the site of the VA origin with the guidance of transvenous epicardial mapping. Therefore, electrophysiological information obtained by transvenous epicardial mapping should be carefully interpreted. OBJECTIVES: This study investigated ventricular activation patterns within the great cardiac vein (GCV) during idiopathic LVS VAs. METHODS: We studied 38 consecutive patients who underwent a successful endocardial ablation of idiopathic LVS VAs at the left ostial process, left coronary sinus, and commissure between the left and right coronary cusps. RESULTS: Twenty-nine patients exhibited a radial activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded around the junction between the GCV and anterior interventricular vein (AIVV). The remaining 9 patients exhibited a septal activation pattern in which the earliest ventricular activation was recorded within the AIVV, with the activation sequence being from the AIVV to GCV. The septal group mainly exhibited left bundle branch block pattern, whereas the radial group exhibited right bundle branch block pattern (P < 0.0001). The distance between the earliest ventricular activation site within the GCV or AIVV and the successful ablation site was significantly larger for LVS VAs with a septal activation pattern than those with a radial activation pattern. CONCLUSIONS: During idiopathic basal LVS VAs, activation from those VA origins often preferentially conducted along the ventricular septum. It should be kept in mind that this unusual activation pattern may mislead the mapping and catheter ablation of LVS VAs.

title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
abstract: Hypertension is an inflammatory disease with the immune system playing a key role in mediating hypertensive outcomes and end-organ damage. The risk of hypertension is greater in men than in women before women enter menopause. After menopause, a woman's risk for developing hypertension increases and accelerates beyond that of age-matched men. Moreover, after menopause, the rate of hypertension control in women is lower than in men. Indeed, cardiovascular drug efficacy in women is different from that in men, with recent studies highlighting serious side effects of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors and β-blockers in postmenopausal women. Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

title: Association Between Peripheral and Coronary Subclinical Atherosclerosis Burden in Midlife.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Atherosclerosis, silent in its early stages, underlies most cardiovascular manifestations. The inter-relation between silent atherosclerosis across vascular territories remains insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to assess the association between peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis in asymptomatic individuals. METHODS: A subgroup of individuals of the PESA (Progression of Early Subclinical Atherosclerosis) cohort underwent contrast-enhanced coronary computed tomography angiography in addition to peripheral (carotid and femoral) atherosclerosis assessment using 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound. Peripheral global plaque volume was calculated as the sum of bilateral carotid and femoral plaque burden using an artificial intelligence-based automated approach. Coronary computed tomographic angiographic images were qualitatively evaluated for the presence and severity of coronary atherosclerosis (percentage stenosis) and quantitatively for coronary artery calcium score (CACS) and global coronary plaque volume measurement. RESULTS: A total of 374 participants (mean age: 55 years, 34% women, 63% with CACS = 0) were included. Peripheral atherosclerosis was present in 75%. Peripheral global plaque volume was significantly associated with the presence, severity, and burden of coronary atherosclerosis (coronary plaque volume) (r = 0.69; P < 0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, and conventional risk factor profile, individuals with peripheral atherosclerosis had nearly 3 times greater odds of having coronary atherosclerosis than those without (OR: 2.66; 95% CI: 1.50-4.72; P = 0.001). Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis remained significantly and independently associated with coronary plaque. Among participants with CACS = 0, noncalcified coronary plaque was detected in 12.0%, nearly all of whom (93%) had concomitant peripheral atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Peripheral and coronary atherosclerosis were strongly correlated in asymptomatic persons. Both carotid and femoral atherosclerosis were associated with coronary artery disease independently of each other.

title: Systematic Transesophageal Echocardiographic Identification of Tricuspid Valve Commissures and Subvalvular Apparatus.
abstract: Transcatheter tricuspid valve (TV) intervention is rapidly evolving and several classes of therapeutic devices are currently in development. The anatomic knowledge of the TV is the cornerstone for transcatheter patient selection, and the successful implantation of the devices depends on imaging guidance. Anatomically, leaflets are separated by the commissures, which have peculiar findings: they are supported by fan-shaped chords and do not open directly into the annulus, but a few millimeters of the leaflet tissue remain, similar to small scallops. While a comprehensive echocardiographic assessment of TV has been extensively reported, few papers have focused on analyzing commissures and their impact on interventions. This paper aims to introduce a novel echocardiographic approach focusing on TV commissures, and provide a dedicated transesophageal imaging protocol and methodology for recognizing their anatomic landmarks. Multiple dedicated transesophageal views are comprehensively reported for each commissure, in order to ensure a guide for emerging transcatheter procedures.

title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association.
abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.

title: Initial Experience with Bachmann Bundle Pacing Lead Implantation as a Rhythm Control Strategy in Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Bachmann bundle pacing (BBP) is challenging during atrial fibrillation (AF) because ECG based endpoints cannot confirm lead positioning. We aimed to demonstrate the feasibility of a practical approach to BBP implantation during AF and propose a framework for comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) for rhythm control in patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy. METHODS AND RESULTS: Twenty-four consecutive patients with persistent or longstanding persistent AF and preserved ejection fraction underwent dual-chamber BBP and LBBP implantation with individually optimized pacing rate and AV interval. Twelve underwent BBP during AF (Group 1) and 12 during sinus (Group 2), including six cardioverted intraprocedurally. During AF, lead positioning was guided by anatomical landmarks, local electrograms, current of injury, and impedance changes. After sinus rhythm restoration, BBP was confirmed in 11/12 Group 1 patients. Reductions in P-wave duration and interatrial block were observed in both groups. Seventeen had been referred for pace-and-ablate therapy; three in Group 1 reverted spontaneously to sinus rhythm before cardioversion. Over a median 192 [139-212] days after sinus restoration, 12/17 maintained sinus rhythm; 2 underwent AV node ablation, 1 AF ablation, 1 repeat cardioversion, and 1 required rate-control medication for paroxysmal AF. No complications occurred. CONCLUSION: BBP implantation during AF is feasible using anatomical and electrophysiological markers, with Bachmann bundle capture confirmed after sinus rhythm restoration. Exploratory findings suggest that comprehensive conduction system pacing with BBP and LBBP may support a rhythm-control (pace-and-wait) strategy in persistent AF patients referred for pace-and-ablate therapy.

title: Heart Failure Phenotyping and Prognosis by CMR-Derived Oxygen Delivery and Extraction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Heart failure reflects impaired matching of systemic oxygen delivery to metabolic demand, yet resting oxygen transport is seldom measured. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to noninvasively derive resting oxygen delivery and extraction using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) and relate these to clinical characteristics and outcomes. METHODS: In this retrospective study, in patients with heart failure referred for clinical CMR, cardiac output was assessed by cine imaging; basal blood-pool T2 mapping provided imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation; and measured hemoglobin enabled calculation of arterial oxygen content. Arterial oxygen saturation was fixed at 96%. We derived indexed systemic oxygen delivery (DO2i), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), and indexed systemic oxygen consumption (VO2i). The endpoint was all-cause death or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (62 events). VO2i varied widely (tertile means 138.8, 207.9, and 293.8 mL/min/m2), while left ventricular ejection fraction did not differ (38.8%, 40.6%, and 40.3%; P = 0.42). Imaging-derived venous oxygen saturation decreased across increasing VO2i tertiles (61.5%, 54.3%, and 50.7%; P < 0.0001). In Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, ejection fraction, and late gadolinium enhancement, VO2i was associated with the endpoint (HR: 1.15 per 50 mL/min/m2, 95% CI: 1.00-1.32; P = 0.046), but discrimination of VO2i alone was poor (Harrell's C = 0.53). Delivery-extraction phenotypes differed in event risk (log-rank P = 0.026): event proportions were 8.6% (high DO2i/low OEF), 14.0% (low DO2i/low OEF), 16.8% (high DO2i/high OEF), and 18.3% (low DO2i/high OEF). The delivery-extraction phenotype remained associated with outcome after adjustment for age, sex, left ventricular ejection fraction, and CMR-derived filling pressure. CONCLUSIONS: In this hypothesis-generating study, CMR-based oxygen supply-demand assessment delineates resting delivery-extraction phenotypes associated with heart failure outcomes.

title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation: PRIME-MR Registry Insights.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR. METHODS: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization. RESULTS: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011). CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

title: Fluoroscopy-Only Versus TEE-Guided Left Atrial Appendage Closure: A Comparison of Disk-Type and Plug-Type Devices.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopy alone is emerging as a guidance modality for left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO). OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of fluoroscopy-only vs transesophageal echocardiography (TEE)-guided LAAO and compared the fluoroscopic views required for plug-type and disk-type devices. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, patients undergoing LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only or by TEE with fluoroscopy were divided into a fluoroscopy-only group (n = 603) and a TEE group (n = 156) and further into a fluoroscopy-only disk-type (FODT) (n = 382), fluoroscopy-only plug-type (n = 221), TEE disk-type (n = 76), and TEE plug-type (n = 80) subgroups. Follow-up included TEE at 3 to 6 months and clinical event monitoring. RESULTS: The fluoroscopy-only group exhibited comparable implantation success (99.8% vs 100%; P = 1.000), peridevice leak rates (≥3 mm: 1.0% vs 1.3%; P = 0.671) and clinical outcomes during follow-up to the TEE group, with significantly shorter LAAO procedure times (40.9 ± 21.7 vs 78.9 ± 35.0 min; P < 0.001). The FODT subgroup required more views under fluoroscopy (3 [3, 3] vs 2 [2, 3]; P < 0.001) despite comparable peridevice leak rates. The clinical outcomes were similar between the TEE and fluoroscopy-only groups and between the FODT and fluoroscopy-only plug-type subgroups. CONCLUSIONS: Whether a disk-type or plug-type device is employed, LAAO guided by fluoroscopy only appears to be as feasible and safe as guidance by TEE. However, disk-type device needed more fluoroscopy views for accurate implantation than plug-type device. In the absence of randomized data, these hypothesis-generating findings should not be extrapolated to less experienced operators or centers.

title: Identifying Plasma Proteins for Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Penetrance and Severity in Pathogenic Variant Carriers and Noncarriers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a clinically variable disease in onset and progression. Pathogenic MYBPC3 variants account for a substantial proportion of HCM diagnoses. OBJECTIVES: This study sought to identify protein biomarkers associated with HCM penetrance and severity. METHODS: Olink-assayed plasma proteins of 144 pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers were evaluated for associations with HCM severity based on diagnostic criteria (unaffected, mildly, or severely affected). Identified proteins were replicated in the UK Biobank considering time to onset of HCM (67 cases), cardiomyopathy (156 cases), and associations with left ventricular maximum wall thickness (6,492 participants). After prioritizing proteins on cardiac tissue expression and druggability, we examined disease penetrance through associations with heart failure (HF) and arrhythmic outcomes in 272 UK Biobank participants with known pathogenic HCM variants free of cardiomyopathy at proteomics assessment. RESULTS: Among pathogenic MYBPC3 variant carriers, we identified 27 proteins associated with HCM severity, of which 22 replicated in the UK Biobank. Six proteins were prioritized (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide [NT-proBNP], growth/differentiation factor [GDF]-15, fibroblast growth factor [FGF]-23, adrenomedullin [ADM], renin [REN], and neural cell adhesion molecule 1 [NCAM1]), of which 5 associated with disease penetrance in pathogenic variant carriers: NT-proBNP and REN associated with increased HF and arrhythmic risk, GDF-15 and FGF-23 with HF risk, and NCAM1 with arrhythmic risk. CONCLUSIONS: Through the integration of proteomic analyses in both clinical and general population cohorts, we replicated and prioritized 6 proteins associated with HCM penetrance and severity. These findings highlight potential plasma-based markers for diagnosis and disease monitoring, as well as promising targets for future therapeutic development.

title: PREVENT Risk Stratification for Intensive Blood Pressure Intervention and Life Expectancy in Rural China: A Post Hoc Analysis of the China Rural Hypertension Control Project.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology guideline adopted the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events (PREVENT) equations to guide antihypertensive treatment, but whether PREVENT risk groups identify patients who benefit more from intensive blood pressure (BP) control is uncertain. We evaluated intensive BP control across PREVENT risk groups in the China Rural Hypertension Control Project. METHODS: We analyzed 21 872 hypertensive adults from 326 Chinese villages. Participants received intensive BP control (target <130/80 mm Hg) or usual care and were classified as low risk (<5%), borderline risk (5.0%-7.4%), intermediate risk (7.5%-19.9%), or high risk (≥20%). The primary outcome was a composite of major cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure, or cardiovascular death). Safety, net benefit, and life expectancy were assessed. RESULTS: Over a median of 3.02 years, intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the low-risk (hazard ratio, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.29-0.97]), intermediate-risk (hazard ratio, 0.58 [95% CI, 0.49-0.69]), and high-risk groups (hazard ratio, 0.60 [95% CI, 0.47-0.77]), but not the borderline-risk group (hazard ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.51-1.26]). No significant treatment-by-risk interaction was observed. Adverse events increased mainly in intermediate- and high-risk groups. Net benefit was favorable across all groups and greatest in the high-risk group. At 45 years of age, estimated life expectancy gains were 0.94 years overall, 0.71 years in the intermediate-risk group, and 1.26 years in the high-risk group. CONCLUSIONS: Intensive BP control was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in 3 PREVENT risk groups, with favorable net benefit across all groups. Absolute benefit and estimated life expectancy gains were greatest among high-risk participants. PREVENT risk stratification may inform intensive BP control in community-based hypertensive populations.

title: Feasibility and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation via the right internal jugular vein: primary results of the VAMPIRE multicenter prospective study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are usually implanted through the femoral vein. The right internal jugular vein (RIJV) approach has emerged as an alternative, but evidence remains limited to retrospective single-centre series. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural success, and 30-day safety of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation. METHODS: The VAMPIRE study (NCT06455566) is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter registry enrolling consecutive patients with a guideline-directed LP indication across 15 tertiary centres in France (May 2024-May 2026). The primary endpoint was major procedure- or system-related complications within 30 days. RESULTS: Of 294 screened patients, 272 (92.5%) underwent a first-line RIJV approach. The cohort was elderly (median age 79 [73-85] years), predominantly male (63.6%), with high comorbidity burden including atrial fibrillation in 51.5%, chronic kidney disease in 34.9%, and cancer in 22.4%. High-degree atrioventricular block was the primary indication in 84.9%; 65.8% of procedures were performed urgently. Successful LP implantation was achieved in 266 of 272 patients (97.8%; 95% CI 95.3-99.2%), with septal deployment in 94.3%. Median procedure time was 30 [25-40] minutes and median fluoroscopy time 2.5 [1.1-7.0] minutes. Major complications occurred in 6 of 272 patients (2.2%; 95% CI 0.8-4.7%; p<0.001). CONCLUSION: In this prospective multicenter registry of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation, feasibility and procedural success were high, and 30-day major complications rate low. These results support the RIJV route as a safe and broadly applicable access strategy for LP implantation. However, dedicated studies are needed to compare safety versus the femoral approach.

title: Impact of age on implementation and tolerability of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Elderly patients constitute a growing proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated the impact of age on the implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in HFrEF. METHODS: TITRATE-HF is a prospective, multicentre registry (enrolment June 2022-February 2024) including patients with de novo, chronic, and worsening heart failure (HF). For the current analysis, HFrEF patients were categorized by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). We assessed GDMT implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes (composite endpoint: first HF hospitalization or all-cause death). RESULTS: The cohort included 980 patients aged <65 years (29%), 1120 patients aged 65-74 years (33%), and 1267 patients aged ≥75 years (38%). At 12-month follow-up, younger patients more frequently received GDMT, with quadruple therapy prescribed in 68% of those aged <65 years, 61% aged 65-74 years, and 51% aged ≥75 years (P < .001). In de novo HFrEF, age-related differences were observed within weeks after diagnosis, with faster and more extensive GDMT intensification in younger patients. Still, rates of treatment downgrades and the distribution of side effects were largely similar across age groups. Significant left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement was observed in all age groups (all P < .001). The use of quadruple therapy at 6 months was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint between 6 and 12 months (adjusted hazard ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.86, P = .002), with consistent associations across age groups (P for interaction = .46). CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with HFrEF received less intensive GDMT. Age-related differences emerged early after diagnosis, with fewer treatment intensifications in elderly patients but largely similar downgrade rates across age groups. These findings highlight the need for improved implementation strategies to optimize guideline-directed therapy and dosing levels in the ageing HFrEF population.

title: Precise anatomical landmark annotation of the cardiac conduction system on cardiac computed tomography angiography.
abstract: BACKGROUND: CTA-based estimation of the conduction system from anatomical landmarks underpins a visualization platform (CARA) used in structural heart interventions and conduction system pacing. OBJECTIVE: To quantify the precision and reliability of the annotation method and the bias of trained readers relative to an expert reference standard. METHODS: The expert who defined the method and 6 trained readers each annotated 8 landmarks representing the sinus and atrioventricular nodes, His bundle course (Point B), left bundle branch origin (Point C), and course of Bachmann's bundle (B2-B5), in addition to the three aortic leaflet nadirs on 50 CTA studies in 3 sessions. Repeatability and reproducibility were assessed, referenced to clinically accepted error margins (2-5 mm). Intraclass correlations (ICC) were computed on heights above the aortic annular plane. 3D bias relative to the expert was tested for equivalence within half the margin. RESULTS: Repeatability SD was 1.67-3.98 mm and reproducibility SD 2.03-5.60 mm; all mean deviations were within margin, with 88.6-97.4% of repeat reads and 71.4-94.9% of reader means within margin. Inter-observer ICC on annular heights was 0.76-0.82 for the atrioventricular and 0.79-0.98 for the atrial points. Shared bias relative to the expert was 0.14-3.24 mm, within margin for all landmarks and equivalent within half the margin for sinus node, Point B, B2 and B3; at B3 and B2, 95% and 83% of the apparent separation was repeatability noise. CONCLUSION: The method meets its clinically accepted margins with millimeter precision and good-to-excellent reliability, and transfers from expert to trained readers with bias within margin.

title: Macrophage Gα Chaperone Protein Ric-8B Exacerbates Atherosclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Macrophage stimulatory G-protein (Gαs/olf)-cAMP signaling promotes cholesterol accumulation and inflammasome activation in atherosclerosis. How obesity-associated inflammation amplifies this pathway is unknown. METHODS: We studied human and murine macrophages, genetically modified low-density lipoprotein receptor-deficient (Ldlr-/-) bone marrow chimeras, and human carotid plaques using biochemical assays and a macrophage-targeted resistance to inhibitors of cholinesterase 8B (Ric-8B)-Gα interference peptide. RESULTS: oxLDL (oxidized low-density lipoprotein) activated Gαolf through OR6A2 (olfactory receptor 6A2) and Gαs through downregulation of phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein (p-GIV [phosphorylated Gα-interacting vesicle-associated protein]); both required Ric-8B. Ric-8B bound nucleotide-free Gαolf and Gαs with high affinity (KD, 21 and 29 nmol/L) through Arg75 and promoted their folding, stability, membrane localization, and cAMP signaling. Disrupting this interface reduced macrophage inflammasome activation and cholesterol accumulation. In Ldlr-/- chimeras, the targeted interference peptide localized to plaque macrophages, suppressed lesional Gαs/olf activity, and reduced atherosclerosis; these effects were absent with a nonbinding control peptide or Ric-8BR75E. In male patients' carotid plaques, plasma IFN-γ (interferon-γ) correlated with macrophage-associated Ric-8B S468/T473 phosphorylation. IFN-γ activated a STAT1 (signal transducer and activator of transcription 1)-independent ERK2 (extracellular signal-regulated kinase 2)-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit pathway that phosphorylated Ric-8B at S468/T473, enhancing chaperone activity. Phosphomimetic substitution lowered the pooled fitted oxLDL EC50 for cAMP generation (11.5 versus 27.7 µg/mL in wild-type cells) without increasing basal cAMP; replicate-level EC50 estimates did not differ significantly (P=0.17). This substitution restored the atherogenic phenotype suppressed by Ifngr1 deficiency in obese, but not nonobese, chimeras. CONCLUSIONS: Ric-8B sustains macrophage Gαs/olf-cAMP signaling and atherogenesis. Obesity-associated IFN-γ enhances macrophage responses to oxLDL through STAT1-independent ERK2-casein kinase 2 α catalytic subunit-Ric-8B signaling, supporting a 2-hit mechanism and identifying the Ric-8B-Gα interface as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Rivaroxaban Inhibits Platelet-Driven NOX2-Dependent Oxidative Injury to Endothelium.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endothelial dysfunction is a hallmark of cardiovascular disease, driven by oxidative stress, inflammation, and platelet activation. We hypothesized that the FXa inhibitor rivaroxaban, alone or combined with clopidogrel, could counteract platelet-induced oxidative injury to the endothelium and preserve endothelial function. METHODS: We conducted a prospective multicenter cohort clinical study in patients on chronic antiplatelet therapy (mostly aspirin) who initiated rivaroxaban, measuring indices of oxidative stress, endothelial function (nitric oxide bioavailability, ICAM-1/VCAM-1 levels), and platelet activation before and after rivaroxaban. In parallel, human endothelial cells were exposed to convulxin-activated platelet supernatants from healthy donors with or without rivaroxaban±clopidogrel, and assessed for NOX2 expression/activity, adhesion molecules, nitric oxide (NO) production, and tube-forming capacity. An ex vivo mouse model of angiotensin II-induced endothelial dysfunction was used to evaluate vascular relaxation responses after incubation with rivaroxaban and/or clopidogrel. RESULTS: Rivaroxaban significantly improved endothelial function in patients and in vitro, as shown by reduced endothelial ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expression and increased NO availability despite platelet-derived oxidative stress. Rivaroxaban also decreased H2O2 production, downregulated endothelial NOX2 expression and sNOX2-dp release, and restored angiogenic capacity in endothelial cells exposed to activated platelets. Clopidogrel alone had negligible effects on these parameters. Notably, adding clopidogrel to rivaroxaban provided no additional endothelial benefit beyond rivaroxaban monotherapy. In an ex vivo hypertensive vessel model, rivaroxaban (but not clopidogrel) markedly improved endothelium-dependent relaxation. CONCLUSIONS: Rivaroxaban effectively preserves endothelial function by inhibiting platelet-induced NOX2-mediated oxidative stress and inflammation. The lack of any additive benefit from clopidogrel suggests that rivaroxaban alone may be mechanistically sufficient to counteract platelet-driven endothelial dysfunction. These findings reveal a novel vasoprotective mechanism for rivaroxaban and underscore its potential clinical value in mitigating vascular injury beyond its established antithrombotic effects.

title: Outcomes Among Patients Receiving Watchman LAAO vs Antiplatelet Therapy: A Report From the GWTG-AFIB Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) was approved for patients with atrial fibrillation who can tolerate short term anticoagulation, many patients are poor candidates for any duration of anticoagulation. OBJECTIVES: The objective of the study was to compare 1-year outcomes among patients receiving Watchman LAAO vs antiplatelet monotherapy. METHODS: We performed an overlap weighted observational comparative effectiveness analysis of postdischarge outcomes among Medicare beneficiaries in the Get With The Guidelines-AFIB Registry who received LAAO or antiplatelet therapy. Cox Regression was used for all-cause mortality and cause-specific hazard models were used for nonfatal outcomes. A win ratio was calculated with the following endpoint hierarchy: 1) all-cause death; 2) stroke, systemic embolism, or transient ischemic attack (TIA); 3) major bleeding (excluding gastrointestinal bleeding); and 4) gastrointestinal bleeding. RESULTS: A total of 1,427 patients who received LAAO and 2,284 patients who received antiplatelet therapy were studied (overall median age 77 years, 49.3% female, median CHA2DS2-VASC score 5). Through the first 45 days, the adjusted risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.26; CI: 0.17-0.41; P < 0.001). Between 46 days and 1 year, the risk for the composite outcome was lower among patients who received LAAO (HR: 0.61; CI: 0.48-0.78; P < 0.001). The win ratio at 1 year was 2.71 (95% CI: 1.92-3.83; P < 0.0001), indicating significantly better outcomes among LAAO patients. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with atrial fibrillation, treatment with LAAO was associated with a lower risk of stroke, TIA or systemic embolism, major bleeding, or death compared to antiplatelet therapy.

title: Prognostic significance of incident microalbuminuria in a real-world population at increased cardiovascular risk: A report from a global federated research network.
abstract: AIM: Despite growing interest in biomarker-based risk stratification for incident heart failure (HF), the prognostic value of newly detected microalbuminuria is poorly defined. This study evaluated its association with incident HF and cardiorenal outcomes in a large real-world cohort. METHODS: A total of 985,367 patients aged 40-80 years at increased cardiovascular (CV) risk but with no prior HF or chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage ≥3 was included from the TriNetX Global Research Network. Patients with persistent normoalbuminuria (UACR <30 mg/g) were compared to those with newly detected microalbuminuria (UACR 30-300 mg/g). The primary outcome was a composite of incident HF or all-cause mortality over a maximum 5-year follow-up. Propensity score matching was performed to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: After matching, 150,250 patients were included in each group. Over a median follow-up of 2.5 [IQR range, 3.6] years, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with a higher risk of the primary composite outcome (HR 1.29 [95% CI 1.25-1.34]), as well as higher incident HF (HR 1.31 [95% CI 1.26-1.36]), all-cause mortality (HR 1.43 [95% CI 1.35-1.51]), HFrEF (HR 1.61 [95% CI 1.51-1.71]), HFpEF (HR 1.37 [95% CI 1.29-1.45]), acute myocardial infarction (HR 1.33 [95% CI 1.25-1.41]), ischemic stroke (HR 1.27 [95% CI 1.20-1.35]) and increased risks of CKD progression to stage 3 (HR 2.80 [95% CI 2.67-2.93]) and stage 4 (HR 4.71 [95% CI 4.11-5.40]). In exploratory subgroup analyses, renal function showed the largest number of nominal interaction findings. CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort of patients at increased CV risk, newly detected microalbuminuria was associated with higher cardiorenal risk, supporting further evaluation of UACR for early risk stratification.

title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

title: Exercise Dose during Cardiac Rehabilitation and Long-Term Mortality: Beyond Program Attendance.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Exercise dose in cardiac rehabilitation is commonly inferred from program attendance or changes in exercise capacity rather than quantified from achieved exercise exposure. This study examined the association between supervised exercise dose and long-term mortality and 12-month hospital readmission in patients attending outpatient cardiac rehabilitation. METHODS: This retrospective study included 1032 patients attending outpatient cardiac rehabilitation, with average follow-up of 6.9±1.7 years. Exercise dose was quantified from 10 959 supervised exercise sessions using metabolic equivalent based calculations derived from session intensity and duration, expressed as metabolic equivalent min week-1. Cox proportional hazards models examined associations between exercise dose and long-term mortality after adjustment for baseline demographics, comorbidities, and functional capacity (6-minute walk distance). Logistic regression examined 12-month readmission. Kaplan-Meier analysis examined survival across quartiles of weekly exercise dose. RESULTS: We observed separation in survival across quartiles of weekly exercise dose (log-rank χ2=20.23, P<0.001). Mortality events decreased across dose quartiles, from 48/258 (18.6%) in the lowest quartile to 13/258 (5.0%) in the highest quartile (208-367 metabolic equivalent min week-1). Higher achieved exercise dose was independently associated with lower mortality risk, although the association was attenuated after adjustment for baseline functional capacity. Baseline functional capacity was independently associated with mortality. Exercise dose was not associated with 12-month readmission. CONCLUSIONS: Achieved exercise dose during cardiac rehabilitation demonstrated a linear association with long-term mortality despite no relationship with short-term readmission. Exercise dose accrued during a relatively brief period of rehabilitation may therefore represent an important and measurable aspect of program participation associated with long-term survival.

title: Environmental noise and cardiometabolic health: a transatlantic perspective.
abstract: Environmental noise is a pervasive but under-recognized cardiovascular and metabolic risk factor. Drawing on prior expert reviews and large-scale epidemiologic and mechanistic studies, this review synthesizes evidence on the burden, major clinical associations, biological pathways, vulnerable populations, and mitigation strategies relevant to cardiovascular health. Road traffic noise is consistently and dose-dependently associated with higher risks of ischaemic heart disease, stroke, heart failure, diabetes, sleep disturbance, and adverse mental health outcomes, whereas for railway and aircraft noise, the evidence base is less consistent, although important associations are increasingly reported. Translational human imaging studies, controlled exposure experiments, and animal models converge on a common pathway in which chronic and intermittent noise exposure activates stress-responsive neural circuits, increases sympathetic and hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activity, promotes oxidative stress, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular inflammation, and may thereby accelerate cardiometabolic disease. Noise frequently co-occurs with air pollution, heat, and adverse social and built environments, particularly in socioeconomically disadvantaged communities, and these combined exposures may contribute additively to cardiovascular risk. These effects are especially relevant in urban populations with nighttime exposure and multiple co-exposures. Despite this growing evidence base, environmental noise remains largely absent from contemporary cardiovascular risk assessment tools, prevention guidelines, and routine patient counselling, representing a missed opportunity for risk reduction. Effective mitigation will require a hierarchical strategy combining source reduction, health-informed urban and transport planning, and targeted individual protection. Reducing environmental noise exposure should be recognized as an important opportunity to protect and advance cardiovascular and metabolic health in the 21st century.

title: Shifting the Pressure-Natriuresis Curve: The Cellular Mechanisms of Female Renal Resilience.
abstract: Female and male kidneys exhibit markedly different patterns of transporter abundance and activity along the nephron, yet the physiological significance of the differences remains incompletely understood. Recent experimental and computational studies suggest that many of these differences can be interpreted through the lens of pressure natriuresis, the kidney's primary mechanism for long-term regulation of extracellular volume and arterial pressure. We review evidence that the female nephron exhibits a transport architecture that may facilitate enhanced pressure natriuresis and greater flexibility in effective circulating volume regulation. This framework provides new insights into sex differences in acute and chronic blood pressure control and connects pressure-natriuretic mechanisms with renal adaptations during pregnancy and lactation, hypertension, and aging.

title: Immersive Reality in Cardiothoracic Surgical Education.
abstract: Immersive reality technologies, including virtual reality, augmented reality, mixed reality, and related extended reality platforms, are reforming how surgeons learn complex anatomy, rehearse procedures, develop technical skills, and manage unexpected or rare intraoperative crises. Cardiothoracic surgery is particularly well suited to these tools because postgraduate training occurs in a high-stakes environment characterized by complex 3-dimensional anatomy, limited operative exposure, minimally invasive/robotic approaches, open communication, and the need for synchronized team performance. Immersive platforms facilitate anatomy education and procedural planning and enable deliberate practice and nontechnical skills training. Although most studies remain small, heterogeneous, and focused on surrogate outcomes rather than patient outcomes, evidence from surgical education and cardiothoracic surgery literature demonstrates that these tools impart improvement in knowledge, confidence, procedural accuracy, and simulator performance. This article defines immersive reality technologies, reviews their educational rationale and emerging applications in cardiothoracic surgery, proposes an implementation framework for training programs, and highlights limitations related to haptics, validation, privacy, equity, and regulatory oversight. The next phase should focus on validation of outcome-linked curricula that integrate immersive simulation into competency-based surgical education.

title: Clinical characteristics and prognosis of heart failure patients referred to cardiac rehabilitation: SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: To assess the referral rate to cardiac rehabilitation (CR), the clinical profile of referred vs nonreferred patients, and the association between referral and clinical events in Spanish heart failure (HF) units. METHODS: The SEC-EXCELENTE-IC registry is a prospective, multicenter observational cohort of patients with HF in units accredited by the Spanish Society of Cardiology. Patients were classified according to CR referral and were followed up for up to 400 days for all-cause death, HF hospitalization or decompensation, and the combined endpoint of death or HF hospitalization, with outcomes analyzed using Cox regression. RESULTS: Of 2236 patients, 219 (9.8%) were referred to CR. Referred patients were younger (65.2  ±  11.7 vs 71.7  ±  12.2 years), more often male (73.5% vs 63.2%) and more frequently had an ischemic etiology (50.5% vs 28.8%), fewer comorbidities and more frequent use of quadruple therapy (59.4% vs 46.0%); 74.4% had HF with reduced ejection fraction (11.9% had HF with preserved ejection fraction, and 13.7% HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction). The lower crude rate of the combined endpoint (HR, 0.75; 95%CI, 0.56-1.01) was no longer observed after adjustment (HR, 0.99; 95%CI, 0.71-1.38), with consistent findings in sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSIONS: CR referral was infrequent and preferentially directed toward younger patients with ischemic HF with reduced ejection fraction, a lower comorbidity burden, and optimized therapy, whereas older patients, patients with multimorbidity, and those with HF with preserved ejection fraction remained underrepresented. The lower crude event rate was no longer observed after adjustment for measured baseline characteristics, and the observational design does not allow conclusions on the effect of CR itself.

title: Habitual Coffee Consumption, Genetic Susceptibility, and Incident Stroke: A Prospective Cohort Study in the UK Biobank.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The association between habitual coffee consumption and incident stroke remains uncertain. METHODS: We analyzed 490 889 UK Biobank participants without prevalent stroke. Average self-reported coffee intake across available assessments was categorized as ≤0.5, 0.6 to 1.67, 1.68 to 3.0, and >3.0 cups/d. Incident stroke was ascertained through linkage to hospital and death registries and self-reported physician diagnosis. Multivariable Cox models and restricted cubic splines characterized associations. Analyses assessed effect modification by CYP1A2 genotype and stroke polygenic risk score and used multiple-imputation and competing-risk sensitivity analyses. RESULTS: During follow-up, 22 579 incident strokes occurred. Compared with ≤0.5 cups/d, adjusted hazard ratios were 0.86 (95% CI, 0.83-0.89) for 0.6 to 1.67 cups/d, 0.92 (95% CI, 0.89-0.96) for 1.68 to 3.0 cups/d, and 0.98 (95% CI, 0.94-1.02) for >3.0 cups/d. Splines showed a nonlinear J-shaped association, with the lowest estimated risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. Associations were broadly consistent across CYP1A2 and polygenic-risk strata, with no significant interaction. Moderate intake was associated with lower risk among participants reporting sugar addition, whereas high decaffeinated-coffee intake was associated with higher risk. CONCLUSIONS: Moderate habitual coffee consumption was associated with lower incident stroke risk, with the lowest observed risk at ∼2 to 3 cups/d. These observational findings should not be interpreted as evidence to prescribe coffee for stroke prevention.

title: Three-year outcomes of balloon-expandable valve-in-valve aortic valve implantation for failed transcatheter versus surgical valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve (TAV)-in-TAV compared with TAV-in-surgical aortic valve (SAV) implantation for failed bioprosthetic valves have been limited to short-term outcomes. AIMS: This study compared midterm outcomes between patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and those undergoing TAV-in-SAV. METHODS: From June 2015 to June 2024, 543 consecutive patients undergoing valve-in-valve (ViV) transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) were identified at our centre. After exclusion of ineligible patients, 109 patients undergoing TAV-in-TAV and 349 undergoing TAV-in-SAV were included. Following propensity score matching, 214 patients (107 per group) were analysed. RESULTS: Three-year all-cause mortality did not differ between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups (hazard ratio 1.06, 95% confidence interval: 0.56-1.98; p=0.867). Similarly, no significant differences were detected in secondary outcomes. Over 3 years, the aortic valve mean pressure gradient was consistently lower and the aortic valve area was consistently larger in the TAV-in-TAV group compared with the TAV-in-SAV group. Concomitant percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and coronary obstruction were more frequent in the TAV-in-SAV group than in the TAV-in-TAV group (22.4% vs 8.4%; p=0.006; 10.3% vs 0.9%; p=0.018, respectively). Post-ViV-TAVI computed tomography analysis showed that the waist level was the least expanded segment in both groups. However, expansion at this level was significantly greater in the TAV-in-TAV group than in the TAV-in-SAV group. CONCLUSIONS: There was no significant difference in 3-year mortality between the TAV-in-TAV and TAV-in-SAV groups. However, TAV-in-SAV was associated with higher rates of concomitant PCI and coronary obstruction, as well as lower valve expansion.

title: Acute pulmonary embolism: long-term cause-specific mortality in a Chinese nationwide registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated cumulative mortality, temporal changes in causes of death, and associated factors in a national registry. METHODS: This registry-based cohort study consecutively enrolled 66 192 acute PE patients from 3223 Chest Pain Centres across China (2018-2023) (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04014972). Mortality was ascertained through national registry linkage. Cumulative incidence functions estimated temporal mortality patterns, while Fine-Gray models exploratorily examined factors associated with cause-specific mortality. RESULTS: At 60 months, cumulative all-cause mortality was 22.41% (95% confidence interval [CI] 21.92-22.91), comprising cardiovascular (CV) (11.84%, 95% CI 11.46-12.23) and non-CV mortality (10.57%, 95% CI 10.22-10.92). Causes of death varied over time: acute PE and ischaemic heart disease (IHD) predominated initially, malignancy peaked at 1-3 months, and IHD was the largest named cause in each interval beyond 12 months. Among CV deaths, IHD was the predominant cause (35.7%); malignancy (43.3%) and chronic pulmonary disease (24.6%) predominated among non-CV deaths. Men had higher cumulative CV and non-CV mortality than women; while women only had a higher proportion of CV causes among deaths. All-cause mortality increased with age (from 11.52% at <55 to 38.51% at ≥75 years); acute PE/malignancy dominated in younger patients, while CV/pulmonary disease prevailed in older ones. Exploratory analyses identified age, Western China residence, and vital signs as factors associated with mortality. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalised with acute PE, 5-year cumulative mortality was 22.4%, and nearly half of deaths were from non-CV causes. Shifting mortality patterns highlight the need to evaluate risk-adapted long-term follow-up strategies.

title: Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity. METHODS: A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes. RESULTS: A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons. CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits.

title: CTA-Guided Anatomical Targeting for Bachmann's Bundle Pacing: First-in-Human Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bachmann's bundle pacing (BBP) is an emerging physiological atrial pacing strategy, but implantation relies on fluoroscopic landmarks and iterative electrophysiological mapping. Whether patient-specific computed tomography angiography (CTA) can facilitate anatomical targeting of Bachmann's bundle has not been investigated. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, safety, procedural performance, and anatomical impact of CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP. METHODS: This retrospective, single-center, first-in-human study compared 49 consecutive patients undergoing CTA-guided BBP with 28 undergoing conventional electrogram- and fluoroscopy-guided implantation. RESULTS: Using predefined electrocardiographic criteria, successful BBP was achieved in 65 of 77 patients (84%) and was higher with CTA guidance (92% vs. 71%; P=0.024). CTA-guided implantation resulted in a different distribution of final lead positions, with more leads at the predefined B2-B3 target than with the conventional approach (76% vs. 42%; P=0.006; odds ratio 4.20; 95% CI, 1.52-11.60). CTA guidance reduced implantation time (median 2.0 [1.0-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-7.0] minutes; P<0.001), fluoroscopy time (0.4 [0.2-0.6] vs. 1.6 [1.1-2.9] minutes; P<0.001), and lead deployment attempts (1.0 [1.0-2.0] vs. 2.0 [1.8-3.2]; P=0.001), and increased first-pass success (67% vs. 25%; P<0.001). In patients with successful BBP (n=65), BBP shortened P-wave duration in all cases (161±13 to 142±15 ms; relative reduction 11.6±4.4%; P<0.001), with similar reductions irrespective of implantation strategy. No acute lead-related complications occurred, and electrical performance remained stable during short-term follow-up. CONCLUSIONS: CTA-guided anatomical targeting for BBP is feasible and safe. Compared with conventional implantation, this anatomy-first strategy improves procedural efficiency, supporting anatomical guidance as a feasible approach to physiological atrial pacing.

title: Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative. The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology. METHODS: 520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features. RESULTS: 50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope. CONCLUSION: The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy.
abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

title: Early outcomes of tricuspid valve replacement in patients with tricuspid regurgitation: the Trisol Early Feasibility Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) could lead to a paradigm shift in treating tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improving patient quality of life. AIMS: We aimed to report the 30-day outcomes of the Trisol Early Feasibility Study (EFS). METHODS: The Trisol EFS was a single-arm, multicentre study that enrolled patients with symptomatic ≥severe TR despite optimal medical therapy to undergo TTVR with the Trisol system via transjugular access. The primary safety endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events, including death, myocardial infarction, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding, renal failure requiring dialysis, and the need for surgery. The primary performance endpoints included technical and procedural success, while secondary endpoints included echocardiographic as well as functional and quality-of-life measures. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients, who were treated with a latest-generation Trisol 12-anchor valve, were included from August 2023 to September 2025. The mean age was 75.8 years (range 62 to 91), 78.9% were female, and 78.9% were in New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV. TR was reduced to mild or less in 87.5% of the subjects and moderate or less in 100% of the subjects. The 30-day composite major adverse event rate was 10.5% (2/19) due to one cardiovascular death and one pacemaker implantation. No other complications were observed. NYHA Class significantly improved to Class I/II (87.5%), and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved by a mean of 13.6±34.6 points. CONCLUSIONS: In this early clinical experience, the Trisol TTVR system demonstrated technical feasibility, overall safety, significant TR reduction, and the ability to improve quality of life and functional status in TR patients.

title: Psychological Assets and Cardiovascular Health in Adulthood: A Mixed Methods Investigation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Psychological risk factors like depression increase risk for poor cardiovascular outcomes but psychological assets like purpose in life are protective and linked to reduced risk of cardiovascular events. However, most assets are investigated individually, and not all have been explored in relation to cardiovascular health (CVH). This study used mixed methods to assess multiple psychological assets and evaluate associations with CVH 12 years later. METHODS: Data came from 2092 participants in the National Child Development Study. At age 50 years, participants wrote open-ended responses describing their futures. Two trained researchers qualitatively coded each response by rating them for 7 commonly assessed psychological assets (1=not at all; 7=very): optimism, purpose, satisfaction, personal growth, agency, enjoyment, and overall positivity. At age 62, CVH behavioral factors (exercise, smoking status, sleep) were self-reported; CVH clinical factors (blood pressure, lipids, glucose, body weight) were measured during nurse visits. Following Life's Essential 8 guidelines, CVH components were combined into total CVH scores. Linear regressions examined associations between each age 50 asset and age 62 CVH scores, adjusting for age 50 confounders. RESULTS: All age 50 assets were positively associated with better CVH scores 12 years later, accounting for sociodemographic characteristics and word counts (p≤0.05). Purpose (b=0.81 [95% CI, 0.33-1.29]) and personal growth (b=0.82 [95% CI, 0.34-1.20]) showed the strongest associations with CVH in fully adjusted models. CONCLUSIONS: Higher levels of most midlife psychological assets were linked with better CVH over time, suggesting multiple paths to health protection. These findings highlight assets that could be prevention targets.

title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research.
abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

title: Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation. METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation. RESULTS: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P=0.01).
